Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the EcoPower Renewables Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you'd like to register for a question, please press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss EcoPower Renewables's results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Development Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. EcoPower Renewables delivered a solid performance in the Q3 2024, driven by strong execution and growing demand for our renewable energy solutions. We are making significant progress on our strategic priorities, including expanding our project pipeline, enhancing our technological capabilities, and strengthening our partnerships.

I'd like to highlight four key aspects of our performance this quarter.

First, our overall performance highlights and key achievements. I'm pleased to share details on our Q3 outcomes, which reinforce EcoPower Renewables' leadership in the integrated clean energy sector—from utility-scale solar and wind to battery energy storage systems and emerging green hydrogen initiatives. Against the backdrop of rapid global electrification, supportive policies like the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act and Europe's REPowerEU, plus ongoing reductions in levelized cost of energy for our technologies, we posted impressive results.

Top-line revenue hit $1.28 billion, a 28% increase from the prior year and 12% sequentially, beating our guidance center by $50 million. This stemmed from a 35% jump in engineering, procurement, and construction services, propelled by bringing online 2.8 gigawatts of solar photovoltaic and onshore wind capacity, highlighted by the 1.2-gigawatt Desert Bloom solar project in Arizona—one of North America's biggest bifacial TOPCon installations, posting a fleet capacity factor of 28.5%. Revenues from our independent power producer assets climbed 42% to $320 million, aided by elevated merchant rates in ERCOT and CAISO, where solar power purchase agreement prices averaged $32 per megawatt-hour amid softer spot markets.

Bottom-line adjusted EBITDA reached $285 million at a 29% margin, up 210 basis points year-over-year, due to manufacturing scale benefits and 15% lower balance-of-plant expenses from regionalized sourcing. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share landed at $0.92, topping estimates by 8%, while free cash flow of $180 million supported $150 million in stock buybacks and a dividend increase to $0.18 per share. Our development backlog hit a record 15.6 gigawatts, up 22% from last quarter, with $12.4 billion in revenue contracted through 2028, providing strong visibility for our 20-25% compound annual growth target.

Operationally, solar milestones included next-generation heterojunction modules from our new 5-gigawatt Ohio plant—eligible for IRA domestic content incentives—reaching 24.1% efficiency in independent tests, surpassing rivals like First Solar's 22.6% thin-film panels. We've delivered 1.1 gigawatts year-to-date, landing deals with NextEra and Duke Energy. Wind assets shone with 95% availability across our 650-megawatt U.S. Midwest onshore fleet, and our pioneering 200-megawatt floating offshore wind demonstration off Massachusetts, in collaboration with Ørsted, succeeded using semi-submersible foundations compliant with Jones Act rules.

Storage growth accelerated as we activated 1.5 gigawatt-hours of batteries, featuring a 500-megawatt-hour four-hour setup with Tesla Megapacks for PJM frequency services. Total deployed storage now totals 4.2 gigawatt-hours at 85% utilization and over 12% internal rate of return. Margins grew to 32% with lithium iron phosphate cell costs down 20% year-over-year to $85 per kilowatt-hour, matching industry projections.

By region, North America drove 62% of revenues, up 40%, thanks to IRA tax credit extensions and hyperscaler data center needs from Google and Microsoft requesting 10 gigawatts. Europe-Middle East-Africa rose 25% to 25% share, with 800 megawatts won in Germany's auction at €28 per megawatt-hour LCOE for hybrid solar-wind-storage. Asia-Pacific at 13% gained from Australia's variable renewable energy mandates, including a 400-megawatt Queensland contract using our perovskite-silicon tandem tech aiming for over 30% efficiencies by 2026.

On sustainability, Scope 1 and 2 emissions fell 45% year-over-year with fully renewable factory power, aligning with Science Based Targets initiative net-zero by 2040. Research and development investment grew 18% to $95 million, securing patents for AI-driven operations and maintenance that cut solar degradation to 0.4% annually, plus green hydrogen electrolyzers hitting 70% stack efficiency in a 50-megawatt trial with Plug Power. We completed the $750 million purchase of AeroWind Tech, gaining 3 gigawatts of turbine intellectual property and reducing China polysilicon reliance below 40%.

These wins set us up to gain market share in a $1.7 trillion opportunity through 2030, per IEA outlooks. We're lifting full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $4.85-4.95 billion, or 24% growth, with EBITDA margins at 27-29%. Forward statements carry risks like delays in approvals and price swings in commodities.

Second, revenue and earnings growth analysis. Let me delve into the drivers of another outstanding quarter. We reported consolidated revenue of $1.28 billion, a 48% year-over-year rise and 12% sequential gain, exceeding guidance by $80 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $285 million, with margins expanding 22% to 22.3%, and diluted EPS at $0.92, up 62% from last year. These figures highlight our dominance in clean tech, powered by worldwide electrification, policy support, and a shift to high-margin tech solutions.

Revenue growth rests on three foundations: project delivery and backlog execution, steady services income, and new lines in storage and advanced photovoltaics. Backlog reached $18.5 billion, up 35% year-over-year, with $4.2 billion added in Q3 from long-term power purchase agreements and engineering, procurement, construction contracts—giving solid full-year confidence.

By segment: Solar PV, 52% of revenue at $665 million and up 55% year-over-year, led with over 3.2 gigawatts DC of N-type TOPCon and bifacial modules installed. Selling prices stayed at $0.28 per watt, up 5% quarter-over-quarter, as U.S.-made modules earned full 50% Inflation Reduction Act investment tax credit adders for domestic content. Highlights were a 1.5-gigawatt Texas utility project with NextEra using 24%+ efficiency modules, and New York community solar under NY-Sun. Margins rose 450 basis points to 28% with cheaper balance-of-system costs from stable Southeast Asian polysilicon.

Onshore and offshore wind took 28% of revenue, $358 million up 42%, from 1.8 gigawatts of turbines, including Virginia Beach's first U.S. 500-megawatt offshore site with Ørsted using 15-megawatt Siemens Gamesa platforms at over 60% capacity factors. Production tax credit extensions and IRA Section 45Y boosted orders. We sidestepped Vestas blade delays under 5% with LM Wind Power options. EBITDA margins hit 24%, from 19% last year.

Battery storage and grid services were 15% at $192 million, up 72%, with 2.4 gigawatt-hours including four-hour LFP packs and AI energy management software. Key was an 800-megawatt-hour CAISO standalone co-located with solar, earning $45 per megawatt-hour arbitrage on duck curve peaks. Revenue per megawatt-hour climbed 18% to $82,000, with virtual power plant software at $120 million annual run-rate, up 90%. Margins led at 32% from CATL and LG offtakes below $70 per kilowatt-hour.

Operations and maintenance plus digital services, 5% at $65 million up 25%, grew from drone inspections and analytics on 15 gigawatts managed. AssetGuard AI cut client downtime 22% for partners like Duke Energy, aiding renewals.

Regions: North America 62% or $795 million, up 52%, with $450 million IRA bookings, half from U.S. manufacturing in Ohio and Arizona targeting 12 gigawatts DC by year-end, ahead of First Solar. Europe 24% or $307 million up 38%, via REPowerEU grants for 1.2 gigawatts hybrid in Germany and Spain, securing €2.1 billion auctions over RWE peers. APAC 12% or $154 million up 55%, from India's PLI solar EPC with Adani Green at 900 megawatts and Australian storage. China limited to 3% for components, dodging risks.

Headwinds like 10% stronger dollar forex and polysilicon swings were offset by 85% hedges.

Earnings grew from operating leverage: gross margins up 520 basis points to 31.2%, lowest COGS at 69% of revenue. OpEx up 22% to $210 million or 16% of sales, R&D at 4.5% for perovskite tandems to 35% by 2026 with Oxford PV. EBITDA up 58%, depreciation $95 million on new assets, interest up $12 million on sub-4% green bonds. Net income $210 million, core EPS $0.84 up 55%, FCF $180 million funding dividends and repurchases.

Growth taps trends: 510 gigawatts global adds per IRENA, solar LCOE $25-35 per megawatt-hour below coal. Levers include tech like floating offshore wind 20-gigawatt pipeline and Form Energy iron-air batteries; U.S. vertical integration at 95% fab use; M&A like $1.2 billion 5-gigawatt-hour integrator buy and Tesla JV for 10 gigawatt-hours.

Risks: policy shifts post-election under 20% chance, 15% backlog delays from queues, California REC softness.

Outlook: Q4 revenue $1.35-1.45 billion up 40-50%, EBITDA $300-320 million at 22-23%; full 2024 $4.85-4.95 billion up 46%. 2025 over $7 billion from 25 gigawatts and 10 gigawatt-hours storage.

Third, capital recycling and asset sale transactions. Before moving on, let's explore our capital recycling strategy, central to growth in this capital-intensive sector. We develop greenfield projects at 12-15% unlevered IRRs, then sell stabilized assets at 6-8% yields to infrastructure buyers seeking predictable, inflation-protected cash flows. This recycles funds into our 15-gigawatt pipeline at higher returns, keeping net debt-to-EBITDA below 4 times.

In Q3, we finalized $1.8 billion in deals, YTD $3.2 billion up 45% toward $4-5 billion annual goal. Lead was a 650-megawatt solar portfolio sale in ERCOT and PJM—12 projects averaging 10 years old, merchant in Texas, 15-year PPAs Northeast, 7.2% cash available for distribution yield. Sold 100% to Brookfield Renewable Partners and OTPP-led group at 13.8 times trailing EBITDA, above 11.5 times sector norm per BNEF, for 9% IRR on 2014-2016 capital.

Also, 50% stake in 300-megawatt Midwest onshore wind to BlackRock for $850 million. GE 2-megawatt turbines repowered to 3.5-megawatt with bigger rotors/blades, capacity factors over 42% from 35%, at 7.5% cap rate via IRA transferability.

Net $1.6 billion proceeds: 65% or $1.04 billion to ready projects like 1.2-gigawatt Horizon Solar + Storage in California at $42 per megawatt-hour LCOE; 25% or $400 million deleveraging 0.3 turns; 10% or $160 million to shareholders, dividend at 3.2% forward funds from operations yield.

Accretive: lifted FY24 adjusted funds from operations per share 8%, 15-20% ROIC on recycled capital over five years exceeding 8-10% weighted average cost of capital.

Market trends favor us: post-rate-hike dry powder from GIP, Macquarie, APG; $120 billion trailing M&A up 30% per PwC. Buyers chase stabilized, contracted, ESG assets; IRA 45X/45Y adds 20-25% value; REPowerEU speeds Europe sales like Ørsted's 1.4-gigawatt to CIP at 14 times.

OEM delays make recycling key; earn-outs like $50 million contingent on ERCOT ISO if thermal retirements boost payouts.

Regions: U.S. 65% or $2.1 billion YTD, Texas/California flywheels, 800 megawatts Q4 including ITC-eligible batteries. Europe 25% or $750 million, Iberia/Nordics like 400-megawatt Spanish PV to Masdar at 7.8%. APAC/LatAm 10%, India rooftop JV to Greenko $250 million, Brazil hybrids next.

Enhancements: Value-Up repowered 1.2 gigawatts with SG 6.XM, 25% annual energy production boost; solar trackers with Nextracker TrueCapture to 85% performance ratio; 40% sold assets with 100-200-megawatt-hour BESS for 15-20% uplifts, DOE loans; green H2 pilots.

Strategy: light-asset model, 20-30% GP stakes retained; funds 5-gigawatt priority with offshore like 1-gigawatt NJ. Risks hedged 85% fixed debt; synthetic NAV from KKR $500 million.

2025: $5-6 billion recycling at 14 times multiples, 18% IRRs, 12-15% AFFO CAGR to 2027, 25% pipeline conversion.

Fourth, policy and regulatory environment commentary. The policy landscape offers massive tailwinds for EcoPower Renewables and clean tech. Governments are unleashing fiscal tools to speed energy transition, dropping solar/wind LCOEs below $30 per megawatt-hour, filling pipelines, and lifting returns via credits and guarantees.

In the U.S., IRA drives $110 billion investments since 2022, 65% renewables per EIA. Our solar/BESS qualify for 30% Section 48E ITC plus 10% domestic adder, IRRs 12-15%; $2.4 billion ITC transferred YTD at par with JPMorgan, Goldman. PTC/ITC to 2032 with 20% low-income adders boost 5.2-gigawatt pipeline NPV 25% in ERCOT/PJM.

Challenges: FERC 2023 cuts queues 40%, but CAISO/SPP backlogs derisked 1.2 gigawatts energy-only; Section 301 tariffs to 50% Southeast Asia modules stabilize prices for our 24.5% Arizona 2-gigawatt TOPCon fab; FAST-41 for NEPA on 800-megawatt Texas repowers.

Europe's REPowerEU/Fit for 55 mandates 45% renewables by 2030, 1-year permitting under 1 gigawatt. Boosts 3.8-gigawatt backlog: 1.5-gigawatt Iberian solar-storage, 900-megawatt Polish onshore via €300 billion fund. CBAM from 2026 at €50-100/ton favors our 85% U.S./EU polysilicon, 15-20% edge. UK AR6 4.2 gigawatts at £44/MWh carries 600 megawatts hybrids at 8-10% levered IRRs.

APAC: China’s plan invests ¥2.3 trillion, but duties shift chains; 1.1-gigawatt Vietnam floating JV with $15.5 billion JETP, 28% tandems for local bonuses. India PM Surya Ghar 10 gigawatts rooftops, PLI ₹24,000 crore for 400-megawatt Rajasthan EPC, 30% capex funding.

Brazil/Middle East: 10-gigawatt auctions, 700-megawatt Northeast wind with H2; UAE/Saudi 20-gigawatt tenders, 500-megawatt Shuaibah BESS at $15/MWh, H2 at $1.50/kilogram by 2026.

Positioning: 95% U.S. bids IRA-compliant with First Solar/Qcells; 100-megawatt/400-megawatt-hour iron-air in California via ARPA-E $350 million. IRENA advocacy on minerals—lithium down 70%, cobalt up 15%.

Overall, $1.5 trillion capex to 2030 per BNEF grows backlog 28% YoY to $18.7 billion, 40% incentivized. $500 million buffer hedges risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah outlined, we had a strong financial performance in the Q3 2024. Our revenue was $1.28 billion, representing a 48% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by increased project commissioning and higher energy production across our portfolio. Our gross margin was 31.2%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $210 million, primarily due to increased investments in research and development and sales and marketing. Our net income was $210 million, or $0.92 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Sarah for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Michael. In closing, I am confident that EcoPower Renewables is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions: Participants may now begin by pressing star 1. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of your N-type TOPCon modules on your project economics?

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, John. Thanks for the question. Our N-type TOPCon modules have been transformative for project economics, particularly with their high-efficiency 24%+ performance and bifacial designs. In Q3, we deployed over 3.2 gigawatts DC, including the 1.5-gigawatt Texas project with NextEra. These modules qualified for the full 50% ITC adder under IRA domestic content rules from our U.S. fabs, holding ASPs at $0.28 per watt—up 5% sequentially—while expanding margins 450 basis points to 28% via lower BOS costs. Overall, they lift unlevered IRRs by 2-3 points to 12-15%, reduce LCOE to $25-30/MWh, and enhance bankability with 85% performance ratios post-tracker retrofits. We're scaling to 12 gigawatts domestic by year-end, outpacing peers, and pairing them with BESS for hybrids that capture arbitrage. This tech edge, combined with vertical integration, shields us from supply volatility and positions us for hyperscaler RFPs.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Johnson:
What are your expectations for grid connection timelines for your upcoming projects?

Lisa Patel:
Good morning, Emily. Grid timelines remain a focus, but reforms are helping. FERC Order 2023 should cut queues 40% for ready projects, and we've derisked 1.2 gigawatts in CAISO/SPP by going energy-only. Our 15-gigawatt pipeline has 85% with interconnection agreements or fast-tracked via FAST-41, targeting 12 months for Texas repowers. U.S. backlog 15% faces delays, but we've mitigated with 800 megawatts queued for Q4 sales post-connection. In Europe, REPowerEU caps permitting at one year for under-1-gigawatt, advancing our 3.8-gigawatt. APAC like Vietnam/India benefits from JETP/PLI speed. Expect 70% of 2025 adds on schedule, with $500 million buffer for contingencies.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions: There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for any closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in EcoPower Renewables. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
